abbreviations.definition: adverse event: any untoward medical occurrence in a patient or clinical investigation subject administered a pharmaceutical product that does not necessarily have a causal relationship with this treatment. An adverse event can therefore be any unfavorable and unintended sign (including an abnormal laboratory finding), symptom, or disease temporally associated with the use of a medicinal (investigational) product, whether or not related to the medicinal (investigational) product.

A double-blind study is one in which neither the participant nor any of the Investigator or Sponsor staff who are involved in the treatment or clinical evaluation of the subjects is aware of the treatment received.
Council for International Organizations of Medical Sciences

A complaint is any written, electronic, or oral communication that alleges deficiencies related to the identity, quality, purity, durability, reliability, safety or effectiveness, or performance of a drug or drug delivery system.
Adherence to all study-related, good clinical practice (GCP), and applicable regulatory requirements.

clinical research physician: Individual responsible for the medical conduct of the study. Responsibilities of the CRP may be performed by a physician, clinical research scientist, global safety physician, or other medical officer.
The act of assigning a participant to a treatment. Participants who are enrolled in the study are those who have been assigned to a treatment.
Participants entered into a study are those who sign the informed consent form directly or through their legally acceptable representatives.

A process by which a participant voluntarily confirms his or her willingness to participate in a particular study, after having been informed of all aspects of the study that are relevant to the participant’s decision to participate. Informed consent is documented by means of a written, signed, and dated informed consent form.
An interim analysis is an analysis of clinical study data, separated into treatment groups, that is conducted before the final reporting database is created/locked.

Investigational product is a pharmaceutical form of an active ingredient or placebo being tested or used as a reference in a clinical trial, including products already on the market when used or assembled (formulated or packaged) in a way different from the authorized form, or marketed products used for an unauthorized indication, or marketed products used to gain further information about the authorized form.
Impact of Weight on Quality of Life-Lite Clinical Trials Version
Equivalent to CDISC term “subject”: an individual who participates in a clinical trial, either as recipient of an investigational medicinal product or as a control
Patient Global Impression of Status for Physical Activity
“pro re nata,” the administration of medication is not scheduled
The act of determining if an individual meets minimum requirements to become part of a pool of potential candidates for participation in a clinical study.
Short Form-36 Version 2 health survey acute form

Treatment-emergent adverse event: An untoward medical occurrence that emerges during a defined treatment period, having been absent pretreatment, or worsens relative to the pretreatment state, and does not necessarily have to have a causal relationship with this treatment.
Impact of Weight on Quality of Life-Lite Clinical Trials Version
Patient Global Impression of Status for Physical Activity

instruments.name: Short Form-36 Version 2 Health Survey Acute Form, 1 Week Recall Version
instruments.recall_period: the Physical Functioning domain assesses limitations due to health “now” while the remaining domains assess functioning “in the past week”
instruments.scoring_or_range: Likert scales of varying lengths (3-point, 5-point, or 6-point scales); domain and summary scores norm based T-scores, mean of 50 and standard deviation of 10; higher scores indicate better levels of function and/or better health
instruments.purpose: assess 8 domains (Physical Functioning, Role Physical, Bodily Pain, General Health, Vitality, Social Functioning, Role Emotional, Mental Health), aggregated into Physical Component Summary and Mental Component Summary

evidence.quote: Short Form-36 Version 2 Health Survey Acute Form, 1 Week Recall Version
The Short Form-36 Version 2 Health Survey acute form (SF-36v2 acute), 1-week recall version is a 36-item generic, participant-administered measure designed to assess the following 8 domains:
The Physical Functioning domain assesses limitations due to health “now” while the remaining domains assess functioning “in the past week.”
Items are answered on Likert scales of varying lengths (3-point, 5-point, or 6-point scales).

Scoring of each domain and both summary scores are norm based and presented in the form of T-scores, with a mean of 50 and standard deviation of 10; higher scores indicate better levels of function and/or better health
2 health component summary scores: Physical Component Summary and Mental Component Summary.
Preferred administration order of these questionnaires is 1. PGIS for Physical Activity 2. SF-36 v2 acute form, and 3. IWQOL-Lite CT.

instruments.name: Impact of Weight on Quality of Life-Lite Clinical Trials Version
instruments.scoring_or_range: All items are rated on either a 5-point frequency (“never” to “always”) scale or a 5-point truth (“not at all true” to “completely true”) scale
instruments.purpose: assesses 2 primary domains of obesity-related health-related quality of life (HRQoL): Physical (7 items) and Psychosocial (13 items); a 5-item Physical Function composite is also supported

evidence.quote: The IWQOL-Lite-CT (Kolotkin et al. 2017, 2019) is a 20-item, obesity-specific patient-reported outcomes instrument developed for use in weight management clinical trials.
The IWQOL-Lite-CT assesses 2 primary domains of obesity-related health-related quality of life (HRQoL): Physical (7 items) and Psychosocial (13 items).
A 5-item subset of the Physical domain – the Physical Function composite – is also supported.
All items are rated on either a 5-point frequency (“never” to “always”) scale or a 5-point truth (“not at all true” to “completely true”) scale.
Preferred administration order of these questionnaires is 1. PGIS for Physical Activity 2. SF-36 v2 acute form, and 3. IWQOL-Lite CT.

notes: Rule 11: the PDF holds one protocol version only, Protocol J2A-MC-GZGI(a) (Amendment a, approved 27-Sep-2021); the SoA (pp 13-18) is from this version. The amendment summary (pp 4-5) records changes relative to the original protocol (21-Jun-2021), e.g. vital signs changed from 3 to 2 sitting BP and PR measurements, ABPM and lipid measurements removed from exploratory efficacy assessments as safety assessments; no separate later amendment is in the PDF. Rule 10: the lab-tests table (Appendix 2, pp 84-87) was checked against the page images of pp 84, 85, 86 and 87; the text layer keeps the two columns (test, comment) in row order and the image confirmed every panel assignment, so nothing changed. Conflicts: (1) the SoA vital-signs note (p 14) lists pulse rate, blood pressure and temperature; Appendix 7 (p 100) lists BP and HR measured by pulse only, no temperature — both recorded. (2) PHQ-9 and C-SSRS sit under the SoA group header 'Clinician-Administered Assessments (Paper)' (p 15; the C-SSRS rows continue the group on p 16), while Section 8.3.3.10 (p 70) calls the PHQ-9 participant-completed. (3) The lipid objective (p 24) is still listed as exploratory while the amendment summary (p 5) says lipids measurements were removed from exploratory efficacy assessments as safety assessments. (4) Appendix 12 (p 111) defines CRP as clinical research physician; the SoA row 'High sensitivity CRP' uses CRP for something else that the protocol does not define. (5) The SoA abbreviation list (p 18) and Appendix 12 (p 111) define 'HBC = hepatitis B virus'; the SoA row uses HBV. (6) The lab-table abbreviation list (p 87) expands UACR as 'urine albumin/creatinine ration'; the SoA list (p 18) and Appendix 12 say 'urinary albumin creatinine ratio'. SoA rows the text does not describe: Glucagon, C-peptide, Pro-C3, High sensitivity CRP, Apo B and Apo C3, Leptin, Cytokeratin 18 appear in no panel and no body section (Section 3 mentions only 'mechanistic biomarkers', p 24); Luteinizing hormone (LH) is not in the Appendix 2 table (only FSH and estradiol under Hormones (Female)); Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) is not in the Appendix 2 table, though Section 8.1 says it is determined by the central laboratory; HIV, HCV and HBV screening tests are not in Appendix 2 — exclusion criteria 33-35 (p 37) name HIV antibodies, hepatitis B surface antigen, HCV RNA and anti-HCV but state no lab or specimen, so no lab_and_purpose entry was made; 'Pancreatic amylase' is listed in the Clinical Chemistry panel only as 'Amylase' (p 85), so no lab_and_purpose entry was made for it. The SoA row 'Symptom-directed physical examination' is not named in Section 8.2.1, which describes a 'brief physical examination' (p 56); the brief examination is recorded with no SoA activity. Lab specimens are not stated per panel in Appendix 2; Urinalysis and Urine Chemistry specimen left null. Hypersensitivity tests (pp 86-87) are event-driven and have no SoA row. Tokens in SoA activity names that no abbreviation list defines: LH, HBV, Pro-C3, CRP (defined only as clinical research physician), Apo B, Apo C3; the SoA row 'IWQOL-Lite CT' is spelled 'IWQOL-Lite- CT' in the SoA abbreviation list and 'IWQOL-Lite-CT' in Appendix 12; 'SF-36v2' is 'SF-36 v2 acute form' in Appendix 12. Instrument versions, modes and recall periods are recorded only where printed; IWQOL-Lite-CT, C-SSRS and Participant Survey state no recall period or mode in the body. Page 118 is an electronic approval stamp page, not protocol content. Updated 2026-11-07 to schema 1.1 (no re-extraction): instruments carry kind.
